Subject: Capacity conversation: Dedicated plan for Q2 spikes

Hey Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. We have a pilot starting May 1 and need a proposal for Dedicated capacity that can tolerate scheduled marketing-driven spikes (expected up to +3x for 2–6 hour windows, 3 times per week) while keeping steady-state costs reasonable.

High level asks from our side:
- Reserved baseline for predictable throughput and data isolation (we can start with a 2-month commitment).
- A fast, small-capacity burst lane for predictable marketing peaks; we prefer ephemeral slabs that are preemptible for cost reasons but must not exceed 300ms 95th latency on text-generation.
- Autoscale/fallback behavior: if burst pool is exhausted, requests should gracefully fall back to a smaller model variant or queue with predictable SLO.

Can you send a one-page proposal with the sizing you recommend and the proposed autoscale guardrails? Procurement will need any contract term drafts and a capacity projection spreadsheet.

Also copying Procurement so we can loop in legal once we have the draft terms.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenova AI

Samira — thanks for the clear ask. Sending a short proposal and open items below; attaching a draft term sheet and our capacity projection template for you to populate if needed. (See attachments: dedicated_terms_draft_v3.pdf).

Proposal summary (rough):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent (permanent dedicated slab) to cover steady-state throughput and KV cache warmness.
- Opportunistic slab (ephemeral preemptible): 4 x A100-80GB equivalent activated on-demand for short windows. Slab attaches to the same model variant and KV cache may be warmed via prefix caching to reduce cold-start penalties.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up with 20s convergence (fast-path autoscale for <10s spikes), linear cooldown of 15m, and a per-customer safetyband: once ephemeral slab is >85% utilized, new requests route to model-fallback chain (same policy we used for Atlas Health pilot).

Open items for sizing confirmation:
1) Expected QPS distribution during marketing windows (we only have the aggregate x3). If you can share the attached projection filled out, we can map to token/sec and refine GPU counts.
2) Latency SLO enforcement: do you want hard rejects if fallback is hit or soft-fallback with degraded model variant?
3) Billing preference: hourly add-on vs transient token-buffer credits — procurement preference noted.

Action items: Monica — can you draft the concrete autoscale knobs (scale thresholds, target_utilization, cooldowns) and a short fallback ordering? Karthik — can you produce an ops runbook snippet describing warm-cache warmup for ephemeral slab (include expected warmup token delta and KV cache copy window).

Samira, I attached: dedicated_terms_draft_v3.pdf and the capacity spreadsheet you sent back with a few placeholder numbers. If this looks directionally right I’ll follow up with a clean SOW and then route to legal for redlines.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity conversation: Capacity knobs + runbook for Zenova

Thanks — quick draft of the knobs and operational notes below. I'm dropping the most important numbers so Legal/Sales can see the tradeoffs.

Autoscale guardrail proposal (suggested defaults):
- baseline_reserved: 8 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv)
- ephemeral_slab_max: 4 GPUs (preemptible)
- scale_up_trigger: sustained 60s above 65% GPU util OR instantaneous queue depth > 25 requests
- fast_path_window: 0–10s (immediate spin-up using warm-prefetch if prefix cache exists)
- cooldown: 15 minutes linear; backoff: 2x per repeated spike until 6h soft cap
- safetyband_threshold: 85% ephemeral utilization -> trigger fallback chain

Fallback chain (order):
1) Route to a quantized model variant (Q4_0) with identical prompt handling (expected 1.4x token latency multiplier, cost -30%).
2) If quantized variant not available, apply queueing with a 10s max wait and a graceful partial-response signal to caller.
3) If queue exceeds 30s, issue a 429 with a human-readable SLO-mitigation message (Zenova_SLO_FAIL).

Warmup / KV cache notes:
- Warmup delta: copying KV caches for a 2-token prompt set takes ~12–18s; recommend a proactive KV pre-warm step triggered when marketing campaign is scheduled (sample hooks via webhook).
- Prefetch: allow a short-lived prefetch window 5m before campaign peaks to reduce cold penalties.

Costing (ballpark, USD/month):
- Baseline reserved (8 x A100): $64k/month (commit discount assumed)
- Ephemeral slab (4 x A100, pay-as-you-go in bursts): ~$22k/month (based on 30–40h of burst use/month)

Related artifacts: https://docs.redwood.ai/shared/zenova-autoscale-sheet and HubSpot deal ZEN-2028-042.

I'll also prepare a 1-page ops runbook to hand to Zenova's on-call; Monica, can you paste the runbook into the SOW doc once ready?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
